subject: CableGate: Preflight Qs & blockstore/network decisions
messages:

Subject: CableGate preflight questions for private K8s deployment

Hi Jasmine / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're starting the intake for the private Kubernetes deployment at our Newark colo (Site NGK-2) and want to capture a few constraints before the scoping call next week. Attached is a short site inventory (rack power, uplink counts, SAN model) — note it's a live document.

Quick summary of what matters most for us right now:
- We must keep inference KV/cache and user logs on-site; no token-level traffic leaves the VPC without explicit permission.
- Two 42U racks allocated; network uplinks are 2x100Gb to our fabric, and there's an existing Brocade SAN (FC) we might use for long-term archives.
- Preferred: separate tenant nodepools for internal workloads vs. customer inference to meet compliance.

Before the call, could you confirm the following so we can prepare our network/security folks:
1) Recommended nodepool mix for 8x A100-class GPUs (balanced throughput + headroom)?
2) Persistent store recommendations for model weights (fast local NVMe vs. shared blockstore)?
3) Any preferred approach to KMS integration for on-prem HSM (we use AWS CloudHSM in other regions but have an on-site Thales nShield).

I'll be on standby to fill gaps. Attaching: cablegate_site_inventory.csv (power, PDU, SAN specifics).

Cheers,
Javier
Ops Lead, CableGate Networks

Subject: Re: CableGate preflight questions for private K8s deployment

Hi Javier — thanks for the inventory; that's very helpful. Looping Laura and Neha for the technical details. Quick answers and items we'll cover on the call:

1) Nodepool mix: for 8x A100-equivalent GPUs we typically propose:
   - 2x "inference" nodepools (3 nodes each) with 1x A100-40GB / node (high single-request latency SLOs)
   - 1x "batch/replica" nodepool (2 nodes) with 2x smaller GPUs or fractionally shared GPUs for background jobs
   - 1x "control/ops pool" (3 medium CPU nodes) for sidecars, autoscaler controllers, monitoring
   Rationale: spreading across pools simplifies SLO-based routing and enables rolling upgrades without mass evictions. We'll discuss affinity labels and pod disruption budgets during the call.

2) Persistent model store: two-tier recommended:
   - NVMe local cache (ephemeral but very fast) for active model shards / KV caches
   - Shared blockstore for durable model weights (we recommend Ceph/RBD or iSCSI-based blockstore with fast staging to NVMe)
   We'll propose a sync/refresh window to stage frequently-used weights to local NVMe to minimize cold-starts.

3) KMS/HSM: Redwood supports integrating with on-site HSMs via PKCS#11 and can run a secure gateway in the customer VPC. We'll need network egress rules to the HSM appliance and service account certs. If you'd like, Neha can share a minimal network flow diagram.

Can we schedule a 60-minute alignment call Monday (Nov 23) 10am PT? I'll draft an agenda and a short checklist.

-Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — Monday 10am PT works. Quick answers to your numbered items:

1) Node counts: the 8x A100s are physically 4 dual-GPU servers (2 GPUs per host). We can re-allocate to 1 GPU per pod or use MIG-like slicing, but currently the fabric team prefers whole-GPU mapping for isolation.

2) Storage: we have fast NVMe on each host (local) and a Brocade FC SAN for longer-term model retention. SAN bandwidth is good for bulk pulls but slower for many small reads; NVMe is required for low-latency model shard access.

3) HSM: we have a networked Thales nShield FIPS appliance reachable from the management VLAN (10.22.10.0/24). It requires mutual TLS to a gateway node in the customer VPC.

Also: PDUs are dual-circuit per rack but limited to 6kW sustained per rack; please confirm approximate per-node sustained watt budget so we can validate power.

Attaching the inventory export you requested.

Best,
Javier
Ops Lead, CableGate Networks

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Javier Ramos <javier@cablegate.io>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CableGate preflight questions for private K8s deployment

Thanks Javier — good details. Per the inventory and constraints, here's a concise recommendation to bring to the alignment call:

Nodepool & hardware mapping (short):
- GPU hosts: 4x servers (2 GPUs each) -> create 4 node objects and label by physical host. Use 1 GPU per pod scheduling for isolation; reserve one host as a hot-spare for maintenance windows.
- Node taints: "dedicated=inference:NoSchedule" for inference pool; "dedicated=batch:NoSchedule" for batch.

Storage architecture:
- Local NVMe as primary working cache (fast path) using a CSI driver (nvme-local or direct-lvm). Configure a short TTL garbage collector for model staging (default 24h, tunable).
- SAN (FC) as cold/nearline: present as RBD/iSCSI blockstore for durable weighs. Use synchronous pulls to NVMe for active models.
- StorageClasses: "fast-local-nvme" (ReadWriteOnce, local) and "durable-fc" (ReadWriteOnce, multi-attach via block-provisioner)

Network & security notes:
- Management plane (control plane + HSM gateway) on a separate VLAN; restrict access to the Thales appliance via a single gateway IP.
- Egress policy: disallow outbound inference payloads; only allow explicit uploads of anonymized metrics to redwood analytics endpoint if approved.

KMS/HSM integration:
- We'll deploy a gateway sidecar that proxies key wrap requests to your Thales appliance over mTLS. For key rotation, propose a monthly cadence; Redwood will provide rotation playbooks.

Power & ops:
- Estimate: each GPU host ~1.6–1.9kW sustained when fully loaded. With 4 hosts plus spare and networking gear, the 6kW per rack constraint is tight — recommend re-checking rack-level PDU distribution or moving network switches to a separate rack.

Next steps (for the call):
- Confirm PDU-level power headroom and whether switches can be re-racked.
- Align on encryption boundaries and whether Redwood should host a primary key in an HSM proxy (we support both patterns).
- Agree on PV retention policy for staged model caches (default proposal: GC after 24h, archive write-through to SAN every 12h).

I've put these notes into a short deployment proposal and attached it for the customer and internal ops review. If all good, Jasmine — can you share the calendar invite and the draft agenda?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Staff Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
